name: Daniel's accusers
charge: Conspiring by law against an innocent man
summary: Unable to find fault in Daniel's administration, his enemies procured a decree forbidding petition to any god or man except the king for thirty days. They used his continued prayer to obtain his condemnation. God preserved Daniel, and the king turned the punishment upon the accusers.
offense: The presidents and princes searched Daniel's conduct for a charge and found neither error nor fault. They therefore devised a law aimed at his faithfulness: for thirty days, petition to any god or man except Darius would be punished by the lions' den (Daniel 6:4-9). They found Daniel praying as he had before and presented his devotion as disregard for the king. When Darius sought to deliver him, they pressed the rule that his decree could not be altered. Their scheme used the form of law to punish a man whose administration they could not impeach.
judgment: Daniel came out of the den without a mark because he believed in his God. The king commanded those who had accused him, with their children and wives, cast into the den; the lions broke all their bones before they reached the bottom.
offenseFull: The presidents and princes searched Daniel's conduct for a charge and found neither error nor fault. They therefore devised a law aimed at his faithfulness: for thirty days, petition to any god or man except Darius would be punished by the lions' den (Daniel 6:4-9).

They found Daniel praying as he had before and presented his devotion as disregard for the king. When Darius sought to deliver him, they pressed the rule that his decree could not be altered. Their scheme used the form of law to punish a man whose administration they could not impeach.

entries.commentary: It pleased Darius to set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom, with three presidents over them, of whom Daniel was first, so the king should have no damage. Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm. He was set in a very high position in government.

The presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom but could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him. He was blameless. This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in. They concluded they could only find something against him concerning the law of his God. -

The presidents and princes assembled and persuaded Darius to sign a firm decree that whoever asked a petition of any god or man for thirty days, save the king, would be cast into the den of lions, by the unchanging law of the Medes and Persians.

When Daniel knew the writing was signed he went home, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem kneeled and prayed three times a day, giving thanks as he did before. The men assembled, found him praying, and reported to the king that Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, regarded neither the king nor the decree but made his petition three times a day. They really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God.

The king was displeased with himself and laboured till sundown to deliver Daniel, but the men pressed that the law could not be changed, so he commanded Daniel cast into the den, saying, thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee. The king already understood why he was under the realm of Babylon and had seen what was going on. A stone was laid on the den and sealed with the king's signet.

The king went to his palace and passed the night fasting, with no instruments of music brought before him and his sleep gone from him. Why would the king be fasting. He rose very early and went in haste to the den, crying with a lamentable voice, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God able to deliver thee from the lions.

Daniel answered that his God had sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths because innocency was found in him and he had done no hurt. The king was glad and commanded Daniel taken up, and no manner of hurt was found on him because he believed in his God; then the accusers, their children, and wives were cast in and the lions brake their bones before they reached the bottom. -

Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages that in every dominion men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God, stedfast for ever, whose kingdom shall not be destroyed and who delivereth and rescueth and worketh signs and wonders. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian. He had a wise and humble spirit, was beloved by the king, could answer visions and interpret dreams, and was of the king's seed as shown in chapter one. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

When the Most High cut off the nations of the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and Israel succeeded them and dwelt in their cities and houses, Israel was to separate three cities in the midst of the land and prepare the way to them. This law goes into accidental death, what the Bible sometimes calls manslaughter. An Israelite who accidentally killed another could flee to one of these three cities of refuge, where the avenger of blood could not seek him out and kill him there to revenge the blood of his nearest of kin.

Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past, means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident. The example given is two men hewing wood, and the axe head slips from the helve and strikes the neighbour that he die: he shall flee to one of those cities and live. The avenger of blood is the nearest of kin, and while his heart is hot he may pursue and overtake the slayer because the way is long. But the slayer was not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time past; there was no premeditation, no intention to kill. Accidents happen, and the Most High put laws in place for when these things happened. If it was for sure an accident, the man is not worthy of death, as the scripture says.

If the Lord enlarge thy coast as he sware unto the fathers, then three more cities were to be added. As Israel grew and possessed more of the land of Canaan, more cities of refuge were established where a slayer could flee from the avenger of blood. The purpose is stated plainly: that innocent blood be not shed in the land which the Lord giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.

This gives the distinction between an accident and intentional killing; this is describing murder. He hated his neighbour and lay in wait for him: he devised a scheme, waited for the right opportunity and the right time, rose up against him, and smote him mortally that he died. The murderer cannot then run to a city of refuge to lay low. Those cities were not established for him; they were established so retaliation did not come on those who accidentally brought harm to somebody. The elders of his own city shall fetch him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him: putting away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel is what makes it go well with the nation.

What is a landmark? It pays to use tools outside the scriptures, because what good is reading the Bible without understanding of the words written in it. The Zondervan Bible Dictionary defines a landmark as an object, stone, or post used to mark the boundary of a field, and notes that removal of landmarks was prohibited by the Mosaic law. The landmark establishes the boundaries of a man's property, where it begins and where it ends. A man who keeps nudging his neighbour's landmark over little by little until he has taken an acre is stealing land; the dictionary notes it was considered equal to theft.

One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin. One man alone saying he saw a theft is not proof; anybody can come and lie and get people put to death, imprisoned, or beaten. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. It has to be clear-cut; two or three solid witnesses, not one solid witness and a shaky witness. We deal with facts.

When a false witness rises up, both men in the controversy stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges of those days. False accusation is real: people will lie on a man to cover themselves, and false witnesses arise among your own people as well, which is part of why the nation fell into captivity. The judges shall make diligent inquisition: they get to the bottom of the matter and find out exactly who is telling the truth, who is lying, and what the facts are. A judge cannot judge a matter off what one person says; each side tells the story in his own favour, so you must examine the whole matter, question both sides against each other, and decipher the truth. Diligent inquisition is what separates a good judge from a bad judge; a lazy or partial judge makes false judgment. If the witness is found false, then shall ye do unto him as he had thought to have done unto his brother. Accuse a man falsely of stealing, and the judgment for stealing comes on you; accuse him falsely of adultery or another sin punishable by death, and you are put to death, because that is what you intended for your neighbour. So is evil put away from Israel.
The judgment is public and it teaches: those which remain shall hear and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil among you.

Thine eye shall not pity: in this time under Moses it was life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law. Christ spoke on this saying, because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge. Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

As snow in summer and rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool. As the bird wandering and the swallow flying, the causeless curse shall not come. A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back. Ecclesiasticus says the same: correction and work are for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back. -

Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you become like him. Many of us have argued with an idiot and been made to look like an idiot; onlookers wonder why you are even arguing with him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. He that sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks damage.

The legs of the lame are not equal, and so is a parable in the mouth of fools. As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he that gives honor to a fool. As a thorn goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools. Like a splinter driven under the skin, it hurts and can take days to work out.

The great God that formed all things both rewards the fool and rewards transgressors. As a dog returns to his vomit, so a fool returns to his folly. Second Peter calls this a true proverb, showing the apostles quoted Solomon: those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning. -

Do you see a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope for a fool than for him. The slothful man says there is a lion in the way and in the streets. As the door turns on its hinges, so the slothful turns on his bed; he hides his hand in his bosom and it grieves him to bring it back to his mouth. The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

He that passes by and meddles with strife not belonging to him is like one that takes a dog by the ears. Ecclesiasticus warns not to strive in a matter that does not concern you. A young lady who tried to break up a high-school fight was grabbed by police, slammed face-first, and left with brain damage; the Bible is a true book. As a madman who casts firebrands, arrows, and death, so is the man that deceives his neighbor and says, "Am I not in sport?" -

Where there is no wood the fire goes out, and where there is no tale-bearer the strife ceases. As coals to burning coals and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindle strife. The words of a tale-bearer are as wounds that go down into the innermost parts of the belly. Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.

He that hates dissembles with his lips and lays up deceit within, so when he speaks fair, do not believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart. Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the whole congregation, put out on display. Luke says nothing is covered that shall not be revealed. Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit; that thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High. -

Whoever digs a pit shall fall in it, and he that rolls a stone will have it return upon him. A lying tongue hates those that are afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin. That flattery is deceit.

verses.text: Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Then said these men, We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.
Then these presidents and princes assembled together to the king, and said thus unto him, King Darius, live for ever.

All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Then these men assembled, and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.

Then they came near, and spake before the king concerning the king’s decree; Hast thou not signed a decree, that every man that shall ask a petition of any God or man within thirty days, save of thee, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions? The king answered and said, The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.

Then answered they and said before the king, That Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, regardeth not thee, O king, nor the decree that thou hast signed, but maketh his petition three times a day.
Then the king, when he heard these words, was sore displeased with himself, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him: and he laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver him.
Then these men assembled unto the king, and said unto the king, Know, O king, that the law of the Medes and Persians is, That no decree nor statute which the king establisheth may be changed.
Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.

And the king commanded, and they brought those men which had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions had the mastery of them, and brake all their bones in pieces or ever they came at the bottom of the den.
If a false witness rise up against any man to testify against him that which is wrong;
Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother: so shalt thou put the evil away from among you.
He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.
His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.
Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

lawsResolved.text: Do not join your hand with a wicked man to be an unrighteous witness.
If a witness is found to be a false witness by testifying falsely against his brother, then he shall receive the punishment that the accused brethren would have received if guilty.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
Deceit and fraud a characteristic of the wicked.
Punishment is the fruit and reward for iniquity and wicked ways (you shall reap that which you sow).
